proposals.relationship: Johnson invokes Chakrabarty’s criticism of universal historical subjects to qualify Genovese’s resistance-to-revolution teleology.
proposals.evidence_note: Own On Agency, 117 and123/note11, identifies the problem of translating African forms of resistance into a Western Marxist trajectory whose endpoint is a liberal individual and rights language. His note explicitly directs readers to Provincializing Europe as a pointed critique of arguments of this kind. This is a bounded argumentative resource, not proof that Chakrabarty originated every objection or a new reading of his book. Existing Genovese critique1609 remains consolidated and exact.

proposals.relationship: Johnson draws on Hall’s discussion of the historical subject when questioning an undifferentiated agent of enslaved resistance.
proposals.evidence_note: Own On Agency, 117–118 and123/note12, asks how differently situated subjects—mother, Christian, Igbo or Blacks—understood their actions, rather than assuming a universal individual slave. The note specifically supplies Hall’s The Toad in the Garden and, from a different perspective, Joan Scott’s The Evidence of Experience. Both resources are retained as distinct contributions; no shared doctrine, direct personal exchange or new original essay reading is claimed.

proposals.relationship: Johnson invokes Joan Scott’s Evidence of Experience as a resource for questioning the assumed subject of histories of enslaved agency.
proposals.evidence_note: Own On Agency, 118 and123/note12, links the question of who acted and in what historical idiom to Scott’s essay, expressly distinguished from Stuart Hall’s perspective in the same note. The resource helps interrogate an unqualified individual slave as historical subject; it does not deny that enslaved people acted, attribute every part of Johnson’s analysis to Scott or establish a personal meeting. Scott’s original essay remains unread in this continuation.

proposals.relationship: Johnson explicitly uses Benjamin’s Arcades Project as a framework for studying how the past becomes active in present struggles over memory.
proposals.evidence_note: Own On Agency,119 and123/note16, proposes reversing a simple past-to-present cultural transmission model by examining how historically situated people select and enforce elements of a shared past. He identifies Benjamin’s Arcades Project, especially456–488 in the1999 translation, and Harry Harootunian’s History’s Disquiet as the theoretical framework. Joint credit remains explicit, alongside differential power by gender, age and origin. Neither cited original nor translation is newly read; no wholesale Benjamin lineage inferred.
primary_locators: On Agency2003:119,123/n16; note continues124 with distinct historical examples

proposals.relationship: Johnson uses Du Bois’s accounts of slavery, empire and differentiated labor as resources for a history of racial capitalism.
proposals.evidence_note: Own To Remake the World,2017, develops sustained readings of The Souls of White Folk, Black Reconstruction and The World and Africa. He treats plantation, counting house and factory as differentiated but interconnected components, retaining racial and geographical distinctions rather than asserting that all white workers benefited equally. Cedric Robinson’s Black Marxism supplies an explicitly acknowledged interpretive route, not hidden sole Du Bois credit. This is Johnson’s specific analytical use in the essay, not proof of the origins of his1999 or2013books or a fresh reading of the cited originals.
primary_locators: To Remake the World2017:paragraphs beginning For Robinson, W. E. B. Du Bois through Uncannily, the most ambitious; saved lines149–170

proposals.relationship: Johnson uses Eric Williams’s account of British emancipation and slave-grown cotton to connect industrial capitalism with continuing Atlantic slavery.
proposals.evidence_note: Own To Remake the World,2017, explicitly invokes Capitalism and Slavery1944 for the shift from colonial sugar interests to manufacturing and cotton, arguing that British emancipation did not remove slavery from British economic relations. This is his attributed use of Williams as part of an argument against separating Manchester from Mississippi; the original1944book and underlying trade statistics are not freshly audited. It is not agreement with every Williams thesis or a claim about a teacher or personal encounter.
primary_locators: To Remake the World2017:paragraph beginning Indeed, the history of capitalism through Raw cotton; saved lines176–178

proposals.relationship: Johnson challenges Davis’s animalization explanation of slavery and emancipation, arguing that it conflates ideological doctrine with enslaved experience.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Brute Ideology2014:130–132 distinguishes what Davis actually claims from a literal assertion that enslaved people were animals, then questions the mass-psychological explanatory frame. Johnson uses Barbara Fields’s doctrine/ideology distinction and a close reading of black abolitionists’ word brute to contest Davis’s interpretation. He explicitly thanks Davis for defining the field, acknowledges the importance of affective harm and retains the achievement of abolition. His is a specific, qualified review judgment, not an independent audit of Davis’s full trilogy, black abolitionist originals or a denial of violence.
primary_locators: Brute Ideology2014:130–132, especially131 doctrine/ideology and132 brute; full review127–132
